Ðis is seo gerædnes þe Eadgar cyngc mid his witena geþeahte gerædde, Gode to lofe ⁊ him silfum to cynescype ⁊ [eallum his leodscype] to þearfe.
Ðis is seo gerædnys þe Eadgar cyng mid his witena geðeahte gerædde, Gode to lofe and him sylfum to cynescipe and eallum his leodscipe to þearfe.
Prolog. Dies ist die Verordnung, die König Eadgar mit Beirath seiner Witan beschloss, Gott zum Lobe und sich selbst zur königlichen Ehre und allem seinem Volke zum Nutzen.
Prologue. This is the ordinance which King Edgar decided upon with the counsel of his witan, to the praise of God and to his own royal dignity and for the benefit of all his people.
This is the ordinance which King Eadgar has enacted, with the advice of his councillors, for the glory of God, and his own royal dignity, and the good of all his people.
This is the ordinance which King Edgar determined with the advice of his councillors, for the praise of God and for his own royal dignity and for the benefit of all his people.
This is the decree which King Edgar has issued with the advice of his councilors for the glory of God and his own sovereignty and for the benefit of all his people.

note.seg: G, A, Ld; om. D.

II and III Edgar are the ecclesiastical and secular sections of a single code. It survives complete in three manuscripts. Two, C.C.C.C., MS. 201 and B.L.Harley MS. 55, are connected with Archbishop Wulfstan, and there was once a version in the part of Nero A. 1 which has entries in his hand, though this has lost all up to III Edgar 3. Readings in these manuscripts alone are suspect as due to his influence. The third complete text is in Cott. Nero A. 1, but in a part which was originally distinct from the Wulfstan part, and which is in a mid-eleventh-century hand; there is also a fragment, Bodleian MS. Vet. A 3 c. 196, a late copy of a twelfth-century manuscript, and this, like the full text in Nero A. 1, is free from the Wulfstan influence. This code is not in the post-Conquest compilations, but it is in Quadripartitus. The place of promulgation was Andover, if IV Edgar (No. 41) 1.4 refers to this code, and the date is not later than 963, the latest date for IV Edgar. The text is edited by Liebermann, I, 194–207; and with English translation by Robert son, pp. 20–9, and Thorpe, I, 262–71.
